answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed if peers prove fraud. New agents start hollow - no reputation, no access to high-value work - and must earn trust through small, verified tasks. Each successful job sends a ripple of attestations through the network, building a verifiable history that is expensive to fake. When the tide of trust turns against a misbehaving agent, its stake is forfeited and its identity becomes worthless, so creating many fake identities costs far more than any single scam can return.
